title: Text and suffix storage is chosen once when a file is opened
body:
`SufrSearch<T>` (`libsufr/src/sufr_search.rs:48`) searches the suffix array in one of three storage modes: the full suffix array in memory, a subsampled suffix array in memory with a `rank` array, or the suffix array on disk through `FileAccess`. It picks the mode with `is_empty()` checks on slices in `search` (L99-131) and in `get_text`, `get_text_range` and `get_suffix` (342-366). `SufrFile::get_text` and `get_text_range` (`sufr_file.rs:296`, `:331`) repeat the same dispatch. `SufrSearchArgs` (L15) and `SufrSearch` have the same nine fields, and `SufrFile::suffix_search` (`sufr_file.rs:852`) builds one per call and opens fresh `FileAccess` handles (863-872).

The query API exists four times. `SufrFile<T>`, `SuffixArrayTrait` (`suffix_array.rs:12`), `SuffixArray32`, `SuffixArray64` and the `SuffixArray` facade each carry `count`, `extract`, `list`, `locate`, `metadata` and `string_at`. The trait exists only to erase `T`, and only `SuffixArray::read` picks the width.

## Proposal

- `index.rs` defines `Index<T>` as header, text and suffixes. Text is `Memory(Vec<u8>)` or `Disk(FileAccess<u8>)`. Suffixes are `Memory(Vec<T>)`, `Subsampled { sa, rank }` or `Disk(FileAccess<T>)`. The mode is chosen once when the file is opened.
- The `~/.sufr` locate cache moves into `index.rs`.
- `sufr_search.rs` becomes `search.rs` and works on `&Index<T>`. `SufrSearchArgs` and `SufrSearch` are deleted.
- `lib.rs` defines `pub enum SuffixArray { U32(Index<u32>), U64(Index<u64>) }`. `SuffixArrayTrait`, `SuffixArray32` and `SuffixArray64` are deleted.

Search results, ranks and extracts do not change.

## Open

Whether the three storage modes are enums or separate types is decided here by counting the cases, under the project's concrete-first rule.
